scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8879: Users in both pods report that no internal portal
loads by NAME anymore -- web0.local through web3.local all fail with
name-resolution errors. Loading a portal directly by its IP address (e.g.
http://10.200.0.3) still works, and pings to 10.200.0.2 succeed. Diagnose.

injection.action: stop the BIND (named) DNS service on dns_server

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: dns_server BIND (named) DNS service
Mechanism: the named daemon on dns_server (10.200.0.2) has been killed, so
  nothing answers on port 53 and every *.local lookup from the pods times
  out -- which is why the portals fail by name. Everything else is healthy:
  the host 10.200.0.2 itself is up and pingable, the OSPF path works, and
  the web servers keep serving HTTP (portals load when addressed by IP).
  The symptom is purely dead name resolution.
Localization: dns_server
Root cause: named not running on dns_server (port 53 closed)
Fix: `systemctl start named` on dns_server
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the BIND DNS service on dns_server (e.g. `systemctl start named`).
Once named is answering again, web0.local..web3.local resolve to their
10.200.0.x addresses and the portals load by name. The web servers and the
network need no change.

bonus-rules-out-network: notes 10.200.0.2 is reachable and portals load by IP, so the network and web servers are healthy -- only resolution is broken

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The `named` (BIND) DNS daemon on `dns_server` (10.200.0.2) — the sole authoritative name server for the `local` zone.

**Mechanism:** Both user-facing hosts (`host_1_1_1_1` and `host_2_1_1_1`) have `10.200.0.2` configured as their only resolver. When they send a UDP/TCP query for `web0.local`–`web3.local`, the DNS server returns nothing because `named` is not running and port 53 has no listener. The clients receive no answer, report `no_addresses`, and the HTTP client gets curl exit code `000` (connection never established). Because no IP is resolved, all four portal hostnames are uniformly unreachable by name — yet direct-IP (`http://10.200.0.3`) and ICMP to `10.200.0.2` succeed normally, because those bypass DNS entirely.

**Localization:** `dns_server` — `systemctl is-active named` returns `inactive`, `pgrep named` returns nothing, and `ss -ulnp` shows no process bound to port 53. No firewall rule blocks port 53; the nftables ruleset is Docker-internal NAT only. No `netem`/`tbf` qdisc on `eth0`.

**Zone configuration is intact:** `/etc/bind/db.local` correctly maps `web0`→`10.200.0.3`, `web1`→`10.200.0.4`, `web2`→`10.200.0.5`, `web3`→`10.200.0.6`.

**Root cause:** The `named` daemon on `dns_server` has stopped (or was never started), making the entire `local` DNS zone unresolvable.

**Fix:** Start the DNS daemon on `dns_server`: `service named start` (or `named -c /etc/bind/named.conf`). No zone-file or firewall changes are needed.

Investigation and writeup together adequately justify the diagnosis and fix.
